resources.string: Phone lock uses this to see which app comes to the front, so it can cover apps during a lock you set in Robot. It never reads what\'s on the screen and never taps anything.
During a lock, every app but calls, alarms and Robot is covered. It\'s a habit you set for yourself, or a rule for someone who will mostly respect it: it isn\'t proof against a determined person.
Locks cover your apps at the times you set.
Phone lock\'s file can\'t be read, so every lock is off.
The file that can\'t be read is kept aside, and Phone lock starts again with no locks.
Enter the lock code to change Phone lock. Turning a lock on doesn\'t need it.
Someone else (a child, a shared phone)
Set a lock code first: locks for someone else need one.
Changes to Phone lock won\'t need it any more. Locks for someone else need a code, so they come back to you.
Forgot the code? There\'s no way to recover it. Outside a lock, Settings › Apps › Robot › Storage › Clear storage removes all of Robot\'s data, the locks and the code included.

When locks started and ended, and anything Robot noticed
Kept for 30 days, on this phone only, never in a backup.
On: Phone lock sees which app comes to the front.
Off: tap to set it up.
On: warnings before a lock, and a notice while one is on.
Off: no warning before a lock starts.
Phone lock is a habit, not a wall
During a lock, the ways to turn Robot off from the phone are covered: Android\'s Settings, app stores, the installer and the launcher\'s menus.

Restarting in safe mode (touch and hold Power off in the power menu): Robot doesn\'t run there. After a normal restart the lock comes back if it is still within its time, and What happened notes the gap.
In safe mode, or outside a lock: uninstalling Robot, or clearing its storage, removes every lock and the code.
Outside a lock: turning off Robot\'s accessibility access or force stopping Robot turns Phone lock off. What happened notes it, and the next lock says it couldn\'t start.
A computer with USB debugging can do anything. On a child\'s phone, turn Developer options off.

The notification shade stays usable during a lock, with its replies and quick settings, because covering it would also cover the lock screen. A picture-in-picture video started before a lock may stay on top.
Phone lock locks only the user Robot runs in, not another user or a private space.
Changing the date or time outside a lock moves Time of day locks with the clock.

Phone lock uses Android\'s accessibility access to see which app comes to the front, so it can cover apps during a lock. It never reads what\'s on the screen and never taps anything. Android will say Robot can “view and control the screen”: that\'s Android\'s wording for every app with this access.

Android calls accessibility access a restricted setting for apps installed from a file instead of an app store, as Robot is: harmful apps installed that way have used it to read people\'s screens. So it can take three steps.
1. Tap Open accessibility settings, find Robot phone lock (under Downloaded apps) and turn it on. If Android says “Restricted setting”, tap OK.

2. Tap App info, then ⋮ (top right) › Allow restricted settings, and confirm; Android may ask for your PIN or fingerprint. No such item? Android isn\'t blocking Robot (perhaps you already allowed it for People): skip this step.
3. Back in accessibility settings, turn on Robot phone lock and tap Allow.
Android may remind you now and then that Robot has this access. Tapping the reminder during a lock shows the cover.
